nodes.summary: A symbol of the token and table stacks that is the name bit $b$ reads as the bit $b$; every other symbol reads as no bit, and so ends a name block.
nodes.title: Reading a symbol as a name bit

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$ and every list $w$ of bits, the clause check of $\varphi$ against the occurrence table of $\varphi$ and $w$ equals the value returned (ignoring the time count) by the formula check of $\varphi$ against $w$ that uses the variable occurrences of $\varphi$, in order, as its variable list.
nodes.title: The clause check on the occurrence table is the formula check

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ and a list $es$ of table entries, the clause check is true exactly when every clause of $\varphi$ contains a literal $(x, p)$ whose live value equals its polarity $p$. Here the live value of $x$ is the value of the first entry of $es$ that is named by the binary code of $x$ and has a value, and false if there is no such entry.
nodes.title: Clause check against an occurrence table

nodes.summary: For every CNF clause $C$, the number of tokens of $C$ is at most the length of the binary code of $C$.
nodes.title: A clause has at most as many tokens as code bits

nodes.summary: The tokens of a CNF clause are the tokens of its literals, in order, followed by the clause-end symbol.
nodes.title: Tokens of a clause

nodes.summary: For every list $l$ of bits, encoding the natural number that $l$ decodes to (Mathlib's binary code of natural numbers, least significant bit first) gives back $l$ if and only if $l$ is empty or its last bit is true.
nodes.title: Canonical binary names

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $n$, the binary codes of $m$ and $n$ (Mathlib's encoding of natural numbers as bit lists) are equal if and only if $m = n$.
nodes.title: The binary code of natural numbers is injective

nodes.summary: The symbols of a table entry with name $q$ and value $v$ are the bits of $q$ as name-bit symbols, in order, followed by one closing marker: the value marker of $b$ if $v$ is a bit $b$, and the dead marker if $v$ is absent.
nodes.title: Symbols of a table entry

nodes.summary: A table entry is a pair of a name, which is a list of bits, and an optional bit, its value; the value is absent for occurrences past the end of the witness.
nodes.title: Table entries

nodes.summary: Given natural numbers $n_0, \dots, n_{k-1}$ and a list $w$ of bits, the occurrence table is the list of $k$ table entries whose $i$-th entry has as name the binary code of $n_i$ (Mathlib's encoding of natural numbers as bit lists) and as value the bit $w_i$ if $i$ is less than the length of $w$, and no value otherwise.
nodes.title: Occurrence table of a list of variables

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula, $w$ a list of booleans, and $n_0, \dots, n_{k-1}$ the variable indices of the literals of $\varphi$ in reading order, with repetitions. The occurrence table is the list of $k$ entries whose $i$-th entry pairs the binary name of $n_i$ (its canonical binary representation, least significant bit first, empty for $0$) with the value $w_i$ if $i$ is less than the length of $w$, and with…
nodes.title: Occurrence table of a formula and a witness

nodes.summary: For a literal $(n, p)$ with variable index $n$ and polarity $p$, the token list is one bit symbol for each bit of the canonical binary representation of $n$ (least significant bit first, empty for $n = 0$), in order, followed by the polarity marker symbol for $p$.
nodes.title: Tokens of a literal

nodes.summary: Let $n = (n_0, \dots, n_{k-1})$ be a list of natural numbers, $w$ a list of booleans and $x$ a natural number. Write $[m]$ for the binary name of a natural number $m$: its canonical binary representation, least significant bit first, empty for $m = 0$. Form the table whose $i$-th entry, for $i < k$, pairs $[n_i]$ with $w_i$ if $i$ is less than the length of $w$, and with no value otherwise. Then the live value of…
nodes.title: Table lookup agrees with the verifier's variable lookup

nodes.summary: Given a list of table entries, each pairing a name (a bit string) with either a boolean value or no value, and a bit string $q$, the live value of $q$ is the value of the first entry whose name is $q$ and which carries a value, or false if there is no such entry.
nodes.title: Live value of a name in a table

nodes.summary: The marker closing a table entry whose value is the boolean $b$ is the value symbol for $b$; for an entry with no value it is the dead symbol.
nodes.title: Closing marker of a table entry

nodes.summary: For all lists $x$ and $w$ of bits, the value returned by the SAT verifier on $(x, w)$, ignoring the time count, is false if the complete length-prefixed CNF decoder fails on $x$, and is the clause check of $\varphi$ against the occurrence table of $\varphi$ and $w$ if $x$ decodes to the CNF formula $\varphi$.
nodes.title: The SAT verifier's answer through the occurrence table

nodes.summary: The symbols of the token and table stacks are a name bit $b$ for each boolean $b$, a polarity marker for each polarity $p$, a clause end marker, a value marker for each boolean $b$, and a dead marker. Equality of symbols is decidable.
nodes.title: Stack alphabet of the SAT verifier

nodes.summary: Write each table entry as one bit symbol per bit of its name followed by its closing marker (the value symbol for its value, or the dead symbol if it has no value), and concatenate these in the order of the list. The table stack is the reverse of this sequence, with the head as the top of the stack, so the first entry lies at the bottom.
nodes.title: Table stack of an entry list

nodes.summary: Given bit strings $x$ and $w$, the tokenizer rejects (returns no result) if $x$ does not decode to a CNF formula. If $x$ decodes to a formula $\varphi$, it returns the pair consisting of the token stack, the reverse of the tokens of $\varphi$ in reading order, and the table stack of the occurrence table of $\varphi$ and $w$.
nodes.title: Tokenizer of the SAT verifier

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ with clauses $C_1, \dots, C_k$ (in order), the token sequence of $\varphi$ is the concatenation of the token sequences of $C_1, \dots, C_k$. The token sequence of a clause is the concatenation of the token sequences of its literals, in order, followed by a clause-end symbol; the token sequence of a literal with variable index $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and polarity $p$ is the bits of the binary…
nodes.title: Token sequence of a CNF formula

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
